_what: Fork w4-ar: AREAS.md rewritten on the co-movement and livestock results - water bodies as management units, what the stations' own behaviour supports, whether the stations are alike, a first grouping along a causal line, administrative water-body numbers, and the cross-water-body correlation as a correlation across management units. With what the rewrite retired.

W4AR-SM-6B.title: Jjokulian, statistical-methods, README: 6b, a grouping claims a shared cause

nodes.label: Co-movement of stations\nsynchrony.json
nodes.detail: data/derived/synchrony.json, written by scripts/synchrony.py from the station panel docs/data/areas/stations_series.* and the positional overlay station_waterbody_overlay.json, with sampling days recovered from the raw CTD file: for each pair of stations, whether their seasonal remainders move together beyond a shift-in-time null, by distance and against the water-body lines.

nodes.label: synchrony.py
nodes.detail: Removes each station's own seasonal cycle, compares pairs with Kendall's tau, judges chance by shifting one series by whole years, pools within-minus-across water-body differences over distance bins weighted by the within-pair counts with a leave-one-water-body-out standard error, and groups stations by Louvain communities of the co-movement network.

nodes.label: Livestock baskets\nlivestock_baskets.json
nodes.detail: data/derived/livestock_baskets.json, written by scripts/livestock_baskets.py from the herd register, the coastal catchment layer, the marine layer and the station panel: stations grouped by the livestock density of the catchments that touch their water body, with random-basket floors at station and water-body level, salinity and depth strata, and repeat-against-between spreads. Area totals only.

nodes.label: livestock_baskets.py
nodes.detail: Places herd records in coastal catchments, links each catchment to the water body it touches along the coast, cuts stations into thirds by the density behind their water body, compares summer medians, and builds the noise floors by shuffling stations and by shuffling whole water bodies.

nodes.label: Herd register\nchr_2024.json (sibling project)
nodes.detail: The register of herd registrations with livestock units (DE), held by the sibling project danish-livestock at data/chr_2024.json. Read in memory by livestock_baskets.py; only area totals leave it.

nodes.label: Herd registrations stand\nfor livestock pressure
nodes.detail: Where a herd is registered stands for where its manure goes, the regulatory unit DE for nutrient, one register year for the decades the stations span, and a catchment's livestock reaches the water body it touches along the coast. Each is wrong in part; where it matters, the comparison is void.

nodes.label: Fluorescence instruments\nnot compared
nodes.detail: The panel's fluorescence is a whole-cast value in relative units. Whether instruments or monitoring programmes differ between the stations of the baskets has not been checked, and nothing held records it per station.

nodes.label: No weather series\nin the co-movement test
nodes.detail: synchrony.py uses the stations' own series only. Whether the co-movement of far-apart stations follows the weather is not tested.

nodes.label: How r was made\ncum_hoc_r.json
nodes.detail: docs/data/lineage/cum_hoc_r.json, written by scripts/areas.py after areas.json: the records r rests on, each step with its code and reason, where each branch ends, the spread, and reruns with one choice changed each. The reader opens it from the number.

nodes.label: areas.py: the two rules
nodes.detail: Pressures go to the nearest kept boundary vertex within the maximum distance, searched to that distance in every direction; bathing stations go to the water body their own wbid names, exactly, and the rest are counted by reason. The cross-area correlation is repeated on each bathing-label period alone.

nodes.label: areamap.py
nodes.detail: Writes docs/data/areas/areas.json from data/derived/areas.json, trimmed to what the map draws: per water body its pressures, bathing observation, streams with their years and the reasons it cannot be modelled; and the cross-area tests.

nodes.label: Methods section 6b: water bodies\nare management units
nodes.said: exist so that someone can be made responsible
nodes.detail: The owner's method: the Danish water bodies exist so that someone can be made responsible for an area and given a target; a number per management unit is about the administration until shown otherwise.

nodes.label: Methods section 6b: a random\nbasket shares no cause
nodes.said: a random basket shares no cause

nodes.label: Methods section 6b: moving together,\nnot similar levels
nodes.said: Similar levels are not a shared cause; moving together is

nodes.label: Methods section 6b: a boundary is\ntested at matched distance
nodes.said: at the same distance apart, do members on the same side

nodes.label: Methods section 6b: two readings\nof failing to beat noise
nodes.said: Failing to beat them has two readings

nodes.label: Methods section 6b: baskets drawn\nalong a causal line
nodes.said: The comparison that tests a grouping draws baskets along causal lines

nodes.said: As an estimator of the ubiquitous

claims.claim: The marine water bodies are management units: they exist so that an authority can be made responsible for an area of sea and given a target for it. Nothing in the data discovered them, and a number computed per water body is a number about the administration until something shows otherwise.
claims.because: The water framework directive has member states set the location and boundaries of water bodies, and the method behind the water plans gives every one of them a requirement; the marine layer is a set of drawn boundaries whose author and basis the file does not record. The stations' own co-movement groups do not reproduce them. The owner's method reads such a grouping as administration until shown otherwise.

claims.claim: Only moving together over time is tested: each station's own seasonal cycle is removed, pairs are compared month by month with Kendall's tau, and chance is one series shifted against the other by whole years, which keeps each series and breaks only the tie in time. A pair moves together beyond chance when it beats its shifted copies at the stated level, so that share of pairs passes by chance alone.
claims.because: synchrony.py subtracts each station's median for each calendar month, computes tau on shared months, recomputes it for every whole-year shift inside the pair's window, and takes p as the share of shifts at least as large; a pair is beyond chance at p no more than ALPHA, with no correction for many pairs.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read: only formatting changed - a methods reference written '6b' now reads 'section 6b', so the compiler reads it as a section reference, not a quantity; no wording changed. 2026-09-12; not yet read by the project owner)

saw.said on AREAS.md: Only moving together over time is tested here, never similar levels. Each station's own seasonal cycle is removed - its median for each calendar month - and each pair of stations is compared month by month on what is left (Kendall's tau). Chance is one station's series shifted against the other's by whole years, which keeps each series intact and breaks only the tie in time. A pair moves together beyond chance when it beats its shifted copies at the 5% level, so that share of pairs passes by chance alone. Distances are straight lines between stations; land is ignored.

claims.claim: For bed oxygen the test can decide only the pairs whose shared window is long enough to shift; the rest are left undecided rather than forced.
claims.because: The counts in synchrony.json: decidable pairs, pairs too thin for the null, and the stations the decidable pairs involve.

saw.said on AREAS.md: **Stations near each other move together far more often than stations far apart.** Of the 515 bed-oxygen pairs less than 20 km apart, 80.8% move together beyond chance; of the 15,115 pairs farther apart, 32.3%.

claims.claim: At the same distance apart, pairs of stations inside one water body move together more often than pairs across a water-body line, for bed oxygen; finer distance bins shrink the gain, so part of it is distance left over inside the bins.
claims.because: within_vs_across_matched_distance in synchrony.json: per distance bin, the share beyond chance for same-body pairs minus that for different-body pairs, pooled with the same-body counts as weights, with a leave-one-water-body-out standard error; and the same over finer bins. The owner's method tests a boundary this way.

confirmed.by: Claude (re-read: only formatting changed - a methods reference written '6b' now reads 'section 6b', so the compiler reads it as a section reference, not a quantity; no wording changed. 2026-09-12; not yet read by the project owner)

saw.said on AREAS.md: **At the same distance apart, pairs inside one water body move together more often than pairs across a line.** For bed oxygen, the share moving together beyond chance is higher inside by 12.3 percentage points, pooled over distance bins (standard error 4.2, leaving out one water body at a time). With finer bins the gain is 9.4 points: part of it was distance left over inside the bins.

claims.claim: Bed salinity, which says nothing about an ailment, gains about as much from the lines as bed oxygen, and more in the size of the co-movement; so the lines follow differences in the water itself, and nothing here shows a shared ailment on top of shared water.
claims.because: Salinity marks bodies of water, not a biological process. If the lines grouped a shared ailment, oxygen would gain from them beyond what salinity gains; it gains a similar amount in the share beyond chance and less in mean tau, by the same pair rule, bins and pooling.

saw.said on AREAS.md: **But bed salinity, which says nothing about an ailment, gains about as much** - 10.7 points (standard error 5.1) - and in the average size of the co-movement it gains more than oxygen: a tau 0.148 higher inside, against 0.096 for oxygen. So the lines follow differences in the water itself, the kind a sill or a fjord mouth makes, and the oxygen gain is no larger than the water's. Nothing here shows a shared ailment on top of shared water.

claims.claim: Stations in one water body are mostly sampled on the same day. On months the two were sampled on different days, same-body pairs still move together more than pairs across a line at the same distance, for oxygen and for salinity, but for oxygen on far fewer pairs and with a larger standard error; with the wider day gap too few pairs remain to answer.
claims.because: same_day_sampling in synchrony.json: the share of pair-months sampled on the same day, within and across; the deciding test rerun with the same-day months removed pair by pair, and with the wider gap in days.

saw.said on AREAS.md: **Part of that could be the sampling trip.** Stations in one water body share a sampling day in 75.8% of their pair-months for bed oxygen, pairs across a line in 24.5%. On months the two stations were sampled on different days, same-body pairs still move together more often than pairs across a line at the same distance - by 21.3 percentage points for oxygen (standard error 10.1) and 15.2 for salinity (standard error 5.3). The gain persists, but for oxygen it now rests on 48 same-body pairs, where the full test had 229. With samples at least 5 days apart, only 10 same-body oxygen pairs remain: too few to answer.

claims.claim: The groups the stations' co-movement draws do not follow the water-body lines: joining every pair that moves together links the tested oxygen stations into one group; its communities are not contiguous, each spans several water bodies, some water bodies are split between them, and they partly sort by the years their stations were measured.
claims.because: graph in synchrony.json: the connected components of the network of pairs beyond chance, and its Louvain communities weighted by tau, with a group contiguous when its stations connect through their nearest neighbours; and the median last year of each group's records.

saw.said on AREAS.md: **The groups the stations draw for themselves do not follow the lines.** Joining every pair that moves together beyond chance links 215 of the 215 tested oxygen stations into one group. Split into communities by the strength of their co-movement (Louvain), they form 5 groups, each spanning between 5 and 58 water bodies; 0 of them form a contiguous patch of sea. Of the 44 water bodies with two or more tested stations, 15 are split between groups. And the groups partly sort by when their stations were measured: one group's records end, at the median, in 2014, the largest group's in 2026.

claims.claim: Distance does not end co-movement: a share of far-apart oxygen pairs well above the chance rate moves together, and it stays with each station's yearly level removed and on months sampled on different days. What moves stations everywhere at once belongs to the whole population: a national signal, not a property of any place in it.
claims.because: share_far_co_moving against the stated level; the same share in the within-year layer and on the different-day months. The owner's method reads what stays stable across the whole population as the ubiquitous part.

saw.said on AREAS.md: **And distance does not end it.** 32.3% of bed-oxygen pairs 20 km or more apart move together beyond chance, where chance alone gives 5%. With each station's own yearly level also removed, 30.1% still do; on months the two were sampled on different days, 29.9%. What moves stations everywhere at once is common to the whole population: a national signal, not a property of any place in it.

claims.claim: For summer bed oxygen, two stations in the same water body in the same month differ about as much as one station from one summer month to the next; any two stations differ more; and the stations' own summer medians spread far wider than they would if the stations were interchangeable.

saw.said on AREAS.md: For summer bed oxygen, one station changes by a median of 1.00 mg/l from one summer month to the next - more than its measurement noise alone, since that includes real change within a summer. Two stations in the same water body, in the same month, differ by 1.01: about as much. Any two stations differ by 1.85. And the stations' own summer medians spread over an interquartile range of 2.27 mg/l, where shuffling which station measured what, among the stations measured in the same month, gives 0.65; 0 of 500 shuffles reached the real spread.

claims.claim: So the stations are not one kind: they differ beyond a station's own month-to-month change, and the differences sit between water bodies rather than within them. That is the first reading, a population that is not uniform, and for livestock the next section shows the grouping does not explain it. Oxygen saturation gives the same answer.
claims.because: Stations in one water body differ about as much as one station a month apart, stations in general more, and the station medians spread beyond the interchangeability null; the livestock contrast does not beat the water-body floor; the readings in livestock_baskets.json give the same verdict for oxygen saturation.

claims.claim: Stations are grouped by the livestock on the land that drains to their water body: the first basket drawn along a causal line, and a naive one. The livestock is where herds are registered, not where manure is spread, counted in the regulatory unit DE rather than as nitrogen, in one register year against station records spanning decades; each catchment is linked to the water body it touches along the coast, a link built here, and an outer fjord does not inherit its inner fjord's land; and low-livestock land is not low-load land, since urban and sewage loads are not in the grouping. Livestock figures are totals over areas of land, never a single farm.
claims.because: The owner's method asks for baskets drawn along causal lines, livestock among them, as a naive first estimate; the caveats are the ones livestock_baskets.py records with its output, which holds area totals only, with totals from too few herds withheld.

saw.said on ARCHIVE.md: A partition is not right or wrong in general; it is predictive *for a variable*. So the question is what the water bodies encode. The statistic, computed within month by `scripts/partition_score.py`, is a ratio of mean squares: the between-basket mean square over the sum of the between- and within-basket mean squares. One means stations in the same basket agree completely. With labels that carry no information both mean squares estimate the same variance and the ratio sits near one half, not zero — so no value in the table below can be read on its own, only its difference from a null.

Latitude stripes are equal-count horizontal bands, as many as there are real baskets, so they keep compactness and equal sizes but ignore hydrography. It is the ledger you need before you can build one: which areas have enough observation to support a claim, which have none, and over which years each stream exists — so that an analysis published in 2025 cannot quietly rest on a relation fitted to 1990–2012 without a reader seeing the gap.
